title: Amplification by independent repetition
statement: Let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester on a finite nonempty domain, and let $P$ be a property of functions from that domain to its codomain. Suppose $T$ has rate $\mathrm{rate}>0$, accepts every function satisfying $P$ with probability $1$, and, for every $\eta\in[0,1]$, rejects each function whose relative Hamming distance from every function satisfying $P$ is greater than $\eta$ with probability strictly greater than $\mathrm{rate}\,\eta$. If $0<\varepsilon\leq\tfrac12$ and $0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$, then repeating $T$ independently $\left\lceil\log(1/\delta)/(\mathrm{rate}\,\varepsilon)\right\rceil$ times still accepts every function satisfying $P$ with probability $1$, and accepts every function whose relative Hamming distance from every function satisfying $P$ is greater than $\varepsilon$ with probability at most $\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: The function domain is finite and nonempty
T is a nonadaptive function tester
P is a property of functions from the domain to the codomain
Every function satisfying P is accepted by T with probability 1
For every η in [0,1], every function farther than η from all functions satisfying P has rejection probability strictly greater than rate times η
